message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data on the current air quality in Los Angeles, but you can quickly check the latest readings from a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to access |
|--------|---------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the AQI (Air Quality Index) for the nearest monitoring station. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles,” and see the live AQI, pollutant breakdown, and forecast. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Many local outlets publish daily air‑quality updates, especially during wildfire season. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., AirVisual, Plume Labs) | Install an app and set your location to get push notifications and trend graphs. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, the AirNow website typically updates every 15–30 minutes, so it’s the most authoritative source for U.S. federal standards. If you need a more detailed breakdown (PM2.5, ozone, NO₂, etc.) or a forecast, AQICN provides that as well.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the AQI values or understanding what they mean for health and outdoor activities!
